title: Boss: the order-processing monster
summary: Refactor a messy order-processing program end to end, keeping every output identical.

steps.title: The monster
body: Here is the program you will clean up. It works, and the business depends on its exact output.
string Process(string cust, string type, List<(string sku, int q, decimal p)> items, string street, string city, string zip)
foreach (var i in items) t += i.q * i.p;
return cust + "|" + street + "," + city + "," + zip + "|" + (t + ship + tax).ToString("F2");

Smells: long method, magic numbers, a type-code conditional, a data clump (`street, city, zip`), primitive obsession, cryptic names. You will fix them in four steps, each checked against the original output.

steps.title: Step 1: names, constants, small methods
prompt: Keep the same signature for `Process` but split it up:
- `decimal Subtotal(List<(string Sku, int Qty, decimal Price)> items)`
- `decimal Shipping(decimal discounted, string city)` using constants `FreeShippingFrom` (100), `StandardShipping` (7.5m), `LondonSurcharge` (2m)
- `decimal Tax(decimal amount)` using `TaxRate` (0.2m), rounded to 2 decimals
- `Process` calls them; the gold/silver discount can stay inline for now
The tests compare `Process` with the original output for several orders.
starter: string Process(string cust, string type, List<(string Sku, int Qty, decimal Price)> items, string street, string city, string zip)
foreach (var i in items) t += i.Qty * i.Price;
return cust + "|" + street + "," + city + "," + zip + "|" + (t + ship + tax).ToString("F2");
solution: decimal Subtotal(List<(string Sku, int Qty, decimal Price)> items) => items.Sum(i => i.Qty * i.Price);
string Process(string cust, string type, List<(string Sku, int Qty, decimal Price)> items, string street, string city, string zip)
var total = discounted + Shipping(discounted, city) + Tax(discounted);
template: {{CODE}}
var dojoItems = new List<(string Sku, int Qty, decimal Price)> { ("A", 2, 30m), ("B", 1, 15.5m) };
Dojo.Eq("Subtotal", 75.5m, Subtotal(dojoItems));
Dojo.Eq("Shipping under 100 in London", 9.5m, Shipping(50m, "London"));
Dojo.Eq("Shipping free from 100", 0m, Shipping(100m, "Leeds"));
Dojo.Eq("Tax", 15.1m, Tax(75.5m));
Dojo.Eq("regular order", "Ann|1 High St,Leeds,LS1|98.10", Process("Ann", "regular", dojoItems, "1 High St", "Leeds", "LS1"));
Dojo.Eq("gold order in London", "Bo|2 Strand,London,WC2|91.04", Process("Bo", "gold", dojoItems, "2 Strand", "London", "WC2"));
Dojo.Eq("big silver order", "Cy|3 Way,York,YO1|136.80", Process("Cy", "silver", new() { ("C", 4, 30m) }, "3 Way", "York", "YO1"));

steps.title: Step 2: value objects for the clump
prompt: `street, city, zip` always travel together. Introduce:
- `record Address(string Street, string City, string Zip)` with `bool InLondon` and `override string ToString()` returning `Street,City,Zip`
- change `Shipping` to take an `Address`
- change `Process` to `string Process(string customer, string type, List<(string Sku, int Qty, decimal Price)> items, Address address)`
Output must stay identical. `Subtotal`, `Tax` and the constants are given.

steps.title: Step 3: polymorphic customer tiers
prompt: Replace the `type` string and its `if/else` with polymorphism:
- `interface ITier { decimal Discount(decimal subtotal); }`
- `class Regular`, `class Silver` (5% off), `class Gold` (10% off)
- `static class Tiers` with `static ITier From(string code)` for `regular`, `silver`, `gold`
- `Process(string customer, ITier tier, List<(string Sku, int Qty, decimal Price)> items, Address address)`
No `"gold"` or `"silver"` checks may remain in `Process`.

steps.title: Step 4: a testable order processor
prompt: Finish the job: turn the methods into a class with injected policy, so new tiers and shipping rules need no edits.
- `interface IShippingPolicy { decimal Cost(decimal discounted, Address address); }`
- `class StandardShipping : IShippingPolicy` with the current rule (free from 100, else 7.5, plus 2 in London)

- `class OrderProcessor(IShippingPolicy shipping)` with `string Process(string customer, ITier tier, List<(string Sku, int Qty, decimal Price)> items, Address address)` producing the same output (tax 20% of the discounted amount, rounded to 2 decimals)
`Address`, `ITier`, `Regular`, `Gold` are given. The tests also use a fake shipping policy.

class Regular : ITier { public decimal Discount(decimal subtotal) => subtotal; }
class Gold : ITier { public decimal Discount(decimal subtotal) => subtotal * 0.9m; }
